about: Builder tips and tool spotlights generated from tools.json verdicts. No quotes, metrics or people. Rotates client-side daily.

posts.title: What should I use to write and edit code with an AI agent?
posts.body: Our current ranked picks for coding agents: #1 Claude Code, #2 Cursor, #3 GitHub Copilot, #4 OpenAI Codex, #5 Windsurf. Quick take on the top pick: Terminal-first agent that handles multi-file changes and long tasks well. Best if you're comfortable in a CLI. Check pricing on each official site before committing.

posts.title: What should I use to go from prompt to a working app?
posts.body: Our current ranked picks for ai app builders: #1 Lovable, #2 Bolt, #3 Replit, #4 v0. Quick take on the top pick: Polished full-stack apps from chat, with Supabase built in. Best pick for non-coders shipping an MVP. Check pricing on each official site before committing.

posts.title: What should I use for my database, auth and backend?
posts.body: Our current ranked picks for databases & backends: #1 Supabase, #2 Firebase, #3 Neon, #4 Convex. Quick take on the top pick: Postgres plus auth, storage and realtime. The default backend for vibe-coded apps. Check pricing on each official site before committing.

posts.title: Where should I deploy my app?
posts.body: Our current ranked picks for hosting & deploy: #1 Vercel, #2 Netlify, #3 Cloudflare Pages, #4 Render. Quick take on the top pick: Best home for Next.js, with instant preview deploys. Watch usage costs at scale. Check pricing on each official site before committing.

posts.title: Which model API should my app call?
posts.body: Our current ranked picks for ai apis & models: #1 OpenAI API, #2 Anthropic API, #3 Google Gemini API, #4 OpenRouter, #5 Groq. Quick take on the top pick: Broadest ecosystem and tooling. A safe first choice for most apps. Check pricing on each official site before committing.

posts.title: What should I use to build my own AI agent?
posts.body: Our current ranked picks for agent frameworks: #1 OpenAI Agents SDK, #2 LangGraph, #3 Vercel AI SDK, #4 CrewAI, #5 n8n. Quick take on the top pick: Lightweight, well-documented primitives for tools, handoffs and tracing. Check pricing on each official site before committing.

posts.title: I can't code (much). What should I use to ship?
posts.body: Our current ranked picks for best for vibe coding: #1 Lovable, #2 Replit, #3 Cursor, #4 Bolt. Quick take on the top pick: The most beginner-friendly way to get a real app with a backend live. Check pricing on each official site before committing.

posts.title: What should I use to make AI video?
posts.body: Our current ranked picks for video: #1 Runway, #2 Google Veo (Flow), #3 Kling AI, #4 HeyGen. Quick take on the top pick: Pro-grade generation and editing tools. The creator favourite. Check pricing on each official site before committing.

posts.title: What should I use for AI voice, TTS or voice agents?
posts.body: Our current ranked picks for voice: #1 ElevenLabs, #2 OpenAI Realtime API, #3 Vapi, #4 Deepgram. Quick take on the top pick: The most natural TTS and voice cloning, plus a voice-agent platform. Check pricing on each official site before committing.

posts.title: Claude Code for coding agents
posts.body: Terminal-first agent that handles multi-file changes and long tasks well. Best if you're comfortable in a CLI. Pricing: Included with Claude paid plans; see site.

posts.title: Cursor for coding agents
posts.body: VS Code-style editor with strong agent mode and tab completion. The easiest daily driver for most builders. Pricing: Free tier; paid plans, see site.

posts.title: GitHub Copilot for coding agents
posts.body: Works in almost every editor and now ships a cloud coding agent. Safe default if your code is on GitHub. Pricing: Free tier; paid plans, see site.

posts.title: Lovable for ai app builders
posts.body: Polished full-stack apps from chat, with Supabase built in. Best pick for non-coders shipping an MVP. Pricing: Free tier; see site.

posts.title: Bolt for ai app builders
posts.body: Fast in-browser builder with a real dev environment. Great for quick prototypes you can export. Pricing: Free tier; see site.

posts.title: Replit for ai app builders
posts.body: Agent plus IDE plus hosting in one place. Easiest path from idea to a deployed URL. Pricing: Free tier; see site.

posts.title: Supabase for databases & backends
posts.body: Postgres plus auth, storage and realtime. The default backend for vibe-coded apps. Pricing: Free tier; see site.

posts.title: Firebase for databases & backends
posts.body: Google's mature backend with great mobile SDKs. NoSQL data model takes some getting used to. Pricing: Free Spark plan; pay-as-you-go.

posts.title: Neon for databases & backends
posts.body: Serverless Postgres with branching. Ideal when you just need a database, not a full backend. Pricing: Free tier; see site.

posts.title: Vercel for hosting & deploy
posts.body: Best home for Next.js, with instant preview deploys. Watch usage costs at scale. Pricing: Free Hobby plan; see site.

posts.title: Netlify for hosting & deploy
posts.body: Simple static and Jamstack hosting with built-in forms and functions. Pricing: Free plan; see site.

posts.title: Cloudflare Pages for hosting & deploy
posts.body: Fast global edge with a generous free tier. Pairs well with Workers. Pricing: Free tier; see site.

posts.title: OpenAI API for ai apis & models
posts.body: Broadest ecosystem and tooling. A safe first choice for most apps. Pricing: Pay per token; see site.

posts.title: Anthropic API for ai apis & models
posts.body: Claude models are top-tier for coding and agents. Strong pick for tool use. Pricing: Pay per token; see site.

posts.title: Google Gemini API for ai apis & models
posts.body: Long context with a free tier in AI Studio. Great value for prototyping. Pricing: Free tier; paid per token.

posts.title: OpenAI Agents SDK for agent frameworks
posts.body: Lightweight, well-documented primitives for tools, handoffs and tracing. Pricing: Free, open-source.

posts.title: LangGraph for agent frameworks
posts.body: Stateful, controllable agent graphs. More setup, but more control. Pricing: Open-source; paid platform, see site.

posts.title: Vercel AI SDK for agent frameworks
posts.body: The TypeScript default for streaming chat and agents in web apps. Pricing: Free, open-source.

posts.title: Runway for video
posts.body: Pro-grade generation and editing tools. The creator favourite. Pricing: Free tier; see site.

posts.title: Google Veo (Flow) for video
posts.body: High-quality clips with native audio. Access depends on your Google AI plan. Pricing: See site.

posts.title: Kling AI for video
posts.body: Strong motion quality at a good price for short clips. Pricing: Free credits; see site.

posts.title: ElevenLabs for voice
posts.body: The most natural TTS and voice cloning, plus a voice-agent platform. Pricing: Free tier; see site.

posts.title: OpenAI Realtime API for voice
posts.body: Low-latency speech-to-speech for building voice agents. Pricing: Pay per use; see site.

posts.title: Vapi for voice
posts.body: Developer platform to ship phone and voice agents quickly. Pricing: See site.
